conventions.convention: The finite alphabet is nonempty and ordered; coupling rows record source masses p and columns record destination masses q. Zero coordinates remain in the alphabet.
Distances are finite real values satisfying separation, symmetry and the triangle inequality; nonnegativity follows from these axioms.
Dual potentials satisfy f_1 = 0 and |f_i − f_j| ≤ d(i,j); the objective is Σ(p_i − q_i)f_i. Positive optimal coupling entries require f_i − f_j = d(i,j).
The chain is indexed from 0 through n, with n ≥ 1; its normalized potential has f_0 = 0, and sgn(0) = 0.
The finitely generated cone allows zero coefficients and includes the empty-support representation of zero; its ambient dimension and generator count are positive integers.

load_bearing.statement: For a nonempty finite metric space and probability vectors p,q, W_1(p,q) equals the maximum of Σ(p_i−q_i)f_i over f_1=0 and |f_i−f_j|≤d(x_i,x_j). Both extrema are attained. For every minimizing coupling π and every maximizing vector f, π_ij>0 implies f_i−f_j=d(x_i,x_j).

For a nonempty finite metric space and probability vectors p,q, Γ(p,q) is nonempty and compact and W_1 attains its minimum. The normalized 1-Lipschitz potential set is nonempty and compact, and f↦Σ(p_i−q_i)f_i attains a maximum on it.
Let r,N≥1 be integers and g_1,…,g_N∈R^r. The set C={Σλ_i g_i: every λ_i≥0} is closed in the Euclidean topology, and αx+βy∈C for all x,y∈C and real α,β≥0.
A coupling of probability vectors p,q on a fixed ordered finite nonempty set is a nonnegative real matrix with row sums p_i and column sums q_j; Γ(p,q) denotes all such matrices.

seams_checked.note: The compact and compact second-countable proofs cite precisely finite primal-dual equality and attainment. They construct nonnegative unit-mass marginals on distinct points of a nonempty finite net before applying the theorem. Restriction and extension preserve the Lipschitz constraint; constant shifts preserve probability-difference objectives. The lifting lemma retains the source-row/destination-column convention, including zero rows and columns. No reverse dependency or stronger finite theorem is asserted.
